newsitem.title: UK: Farmers to meet world food needs in 2020.
newsitem.headline: Farmers to meet world food needs in 2020.

text.p: Farmers will be able to grow enough to feed the world's population in the year 2020, according to Professor Tim Dyson of the London School of Economics.
Dyson, who specialises in population studies, foresees a world population by 2020 of almost eight billion and world cereal demand of nearly three billion tonnes.

Speaking to the Oxford Farming Conference, he said that a continuation of recent yield trends would be enough to produce most of this grain, although he noted that global nitrogen application would have to roughly double to do it.
"There is no alternative to this for farmers in much of the world," he said.

Dyson stressed that although world demand would match world supply, the same did not apply at regional level. There would, therefore, have to be a trebling of world cereal trade, from its current level of roughly 130 million tonnes per year, he said.
